content.text: preop alt: doxazosin 1 to 32 mg PO QD; doxazosin may be equally effective but better tolerated; start a BB only after adequate α-blockade.

CI: hypersensitivity to doxazosin, other quinazolines (ex, prazosin, terazosin), or any of its components. Postural hypotension w/ or w/o Sx (ex, dizziness) may develop w.in a few hrs after dosing; potential for syncope, esp after the initial dose or a dose increase. Concomitant PDE-5 inhibitor can result in additive BP lowering and Sxtomatic hypotension. IFIS observed during cataract surg in some pts on or previously treated w/ alpha1 blockers. ⍉apparent benefit of stopping alpha1 blocker therapy b4 cataract surg. R/o prostate CA b4 starting therapy for BPH. Priapism (painful erection sustained for hrs, unrelieved by intercourse or masturbation) assoc w/ doxazosin; can lead to permanent impotence if ⍉promptly treated. Strong CYP3A inhibitors may ↑ doxazosin exposure and risk of hypotension; monitor BP and for hypotension Sx. Severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh Class C) ⍉recommended; monitor BP and hypotension Sx in Child-Pugh Class A and B. Following the initial dose and each dose increase, monitor BP for at least 6 h. If discontinued for several days, restart therapy using the initial dosing regimen. Most commonly reported adverse rxns: fatigue, malaise, hypotension, and dizziness. OD: most likely manifestation = hypotension; usual tx = IV fluid infusion; dialysis ⍉indicated (highly protein bound).
